Welcome to the lecture webpage for **Research Approaches II: Data Analysis**  (course: [Research Trends in Toxicology (mi8016)](https://www.su.se/english/education/course-catalogue/mi/mi8016)). This lecture reproduces the figures from two toxicology papers about [PFOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfluorooctanesulfonic_acid):

1. [Figure 1F](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00204-017-2077-8/figures/1) and [figure 3](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00204-017-2077-8/figures/3) from paper [PFOS induces proliferation, cell-cycle progression, and malignant phenotype in human breast epithelial cells, 2018](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00204-017-2077-8) (_PFOS phenotype paper_).
2. [Figures 1](https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S0048969724050137-gr1_lrg.jpg) and [figure 3](https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S0048969724050137-gr3_lrg.jpg) from paper [Perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) induced cancer related DNA methylation alterations in human breast cells: A whole genome methylome study, 2024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2024.174864) (_PFOS EM-seq paper_).

The whole lecture will be ran in R. Make sure you have the following packages installed:

+ ggplot2
+ forcats
+ ggsignif
+ ggpattern

```r
install.packages(c(
	"ggplot2",
	"forcats",
	"ggsignif",
	"ggpattern"
))
```

::: {.callout-important}
An R tutorial can be found [here](docs/r_tutorial.md). If you are new to R, make sure you go through this tutorial before the lecture
:::
